text: Hi.
I'm Dr. Emily Glasgow, senior director
of academics at Portland Public Schools.
I'm going to talk about what factors we
consider as we make right-sizing
recommendations to stabilize our
district for the future of our students.
Here's our guiding principle.
How will the changes improve students'
access to educational supports,
resources, and programming in safe and
healthy learning environments?
The answer starts with enrollment.
Every school needs enough students for
solid staffing, resources, and
sustainability.
For K-5 schools, that means roughly 360
students.
For K-8 and middle schools, that's
roughly 500 students.
We also take into account the condition
of each building and its capacity. As
you know, we have many aging buildings
that need considerable work, and we give
preference to the building in better
condition with better facilities.
We also know our dual language immersion
programs are vital to many students and
families.
We may consolidate some of them so we
can continue to offer strong language
programs into the future.
Geography is another key factor.
We want to keep families close to their
schools and limit their travel time.
And finally, it's very important that we
keep the students together with their
classmates as much as possible if we
need to move them to another school.
I hope this adds to your understanding
of how we're making recommendations to
balance enrollment and resources and to
create a stable and sustainable future
for our students.
Thank you.
